items.title: Total Return Investors Better Open Their Eyes About Pepsi
items.summary: PepsiCo raised prices on chips and sodas shortly after cutting them to win back shoppers, and that reversal now sits at the center of a debate over whether the stock deserves a place in a total-return portfolio or a spot on the sidelines.

items.title: 5 ‘Bulletproof’ Dividend Kings Boomers Should Buy Now Before the Market Shifts
items.summary: Rising rates have boomers flocking to Treasuries, but five battle-tested dividend payers with 50-plus years of consecutive increases may offer something bonds simply cannot deliver.

items.title: Coca-Cola’s Secret Weapon Isn’t Its Soda
items.summary: Coca-Cola has beaten earnings five straight quarters and raised its guidance, yet a pending IRS ruling and a price-to-free-cash-flow ratio of 71 hang over the stock like a storm cloud. Here is what the bulls are betting the bears have wrong.

items.title: PepsiCo Walks a Tightrope: Dividend Growth Meets Operating Cash Flow Squeeze
items.summary: PepsiCo just handed shareholders another dividend raise even as profits fell sharply, and the real question is not whether the payout is safe today but whether the cash engine behind it can survive what comes next.

items.title: Pepsi Just Extended Its Dividend Streak Again. Here's the Annual Income on $10,000.
items.summary: A 4% hike in July brings the stock's forward yield to 4.6%.

items.title: Bear of the Day: Yum! Brands (YUM)
items.summary: A stretched consumer backdrop and a food-safety overhang remind us how quickly brand equity can wobble.

items.title: PepsiCo Just Got a 19% Price-Target Cut Ahead of Earnings
items.summary: J.P. Morgan downgraded PepsiCo as weakness in its North American snack business threatens to keep pressure on growth estimates.

items.title: Pepsi vs. Coke: This Is How Much You Could Make by 2031
items.summary: Coke is outpacing Pepsi by a wide margin this year, but one projected scenario shows the losing stock actually protecting your money better by 2031. The answer depends entirely on how much downside you can afford.
